title: Implement provider-neutral rule and judgment interfaces
summary: Create one evaluator contract for deterministic functions and future semantic providers. Make unknown, disagreement, and execution failure explicit so downstream policy cannot mistake unavailable judgment for no important concern.
in_scope: Immutable rule definitions and binding registry
Deterministic adapter and recorded external results
implementation: Implement versioned proposition, eligibility, precondition, and output-implication definitions.
Expose a binding interface that returns receipts and proposals without mutable core access.
Separate execution_status, evaluation_status, semantic_output, and qualification_status.
Validate output labels, cited IDs, admissible states, and consequence permissions before downstream use.

acceptance.criterion: A timeout cannot satisfy a negative semantic prerequisite.
acceptance.verification: Feed a fake timeout into a required downstream judgment.

acceptance.criterion: Deterministic and recorded semantic bindings share one neutral input contract.
acceptance.verification: Run packet validation through both bindings without application fields.

acceptance.criterion: Unknown output labels and nonexistent evidence IDs are refused.
acceptance.verification: Exercise structurally plausible but semantically invalid responses.

tests: Insufficient evidence may be completed execution with no conclusion.
A qualified score cannot grant transition authority.
Independent partial results survive another component failing.
risks: A single success boolean would erase distinctions required for honest composition.

reuse.application: Use focused questions and qualification as provider-neutral evaluator concepts.
